canonical_schema.compatibility: This contract reuses the frozen memory_status and knowledge_type value sets. It does not alter the canonical schema or promote any pending host mapping.

boundary.transport: One JSON object per JSONL line, wrapped by an authenticated import request

constraints: SHA-256 of the supplied source manifest

source_manifest.data_rc_sha256: Exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 JSONL bytes submitted in this request.
source_manifest.record_count: Strict positive integer equal to the number of submitted JSONL records.

constraints: set by Main authentication middleware, not trusted from an unsigned JSONL record

request_envelope.authorization: Main resolves authenticated_principal to its permitted user scope before reading any record. A record user_id outside that scope is rejected.
request_envelope.manifest_integrity: Main serializes source_manifest using RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme, UTF-8 encodes those canonical bytes, and requires their SHA-256 to equal source_manifest_sha256. Main also hashes the exact submitted JSONL byte stream and requires it to equal source_manifest.data_rc_sha256, then verifies record_count before importing any record.

boundary.unknown_input_policy_detail: The request envelope, each record, and nested source descriptor reject unknown fields. Unknown enum values, missing required fields, malformed IDs, cross-user references, and unadmitted sources are rejected without a partial write for that record.

data_record_id.meaning: Data-local traceability key; it is never a production identity.

user_id.meaning: Owner isolation key. The importer rejects a claimed user outside its trusted scope.

knowledge_type.meaning: Frozen Canonical knowledge subtype; primary_category cannot replace it.

memory_status.meaning: A newly imported Data RC enters Main as candidate. Lifecycle promotion, expiry, supersession, and removal are Main-controlled transitions.

scope.meaning: This v1 import is user-scoped only; global or cross-user imports are rejected.

constraints: must pass the production sensitive-content and projection policy

content.meaning: V1 structured knowledge payload persisted through the Main repository ingress. Fields outside this allowlist are rejected; a future content schema requires a new contract version.

confidence.meaning: Producer confidence supplied to the Main repository ingress.

constraints: must name an existing Main source event owned by user_id
must equal the registered immutable source reference for source_event_id

source.meaning: Reference to an existing, admitted Main source event. Main does not create source events through this KB import contract; it rejects a missing, cross-user, unadmitted, or descriptor-mismatched event.

constraints: stable for every retry of one logical record import
unique for a distinct logical record within a user scope
idempotency_key.meaning: Data-supplied retry key. It is the only producer key that Main uses to recover an already allocated production identity.

forbidden_input_fields.knowledge_id: Only Main may allocate a production knowledge_id. Data must not supply, derive, or assume one.
forbidden_input_fields.memory_id: SQLite-derived production identity; supplied values are rejected.
forbidden_input_fields.version_id: Main-derived current content/index version identity; supplied values are rejected.
forbidden_input_fields.version: Main-controlled content/index version; supplied values are rejected.
forbidden_input_fields.production_id: No alias may bypass Main production identity allocation.

required_output_fields.data_record_id: Echo of the accepted producer traceability key.
required_output_fields.accepted: Always true for an accepted record.
required_output_fields.knowledge_id: Opaque production business identity allocated by Main trusted ingress; stable for the logical knowledge item and unique per user.
required_output_fields.memory_id: Canonical decimal-string representation of memory_entries.id for the same user and knowledge_id.
required_output_fields.accepted_version: Positive integer content/index version from memory_entries.version at the first successful import acceptance. It is an immutable acceptance-receipt snapshot, not a current-state field.
required_output_fields.accepted_version_id: Canonical string v<accepted_version> stored at first successful import acceptance; for example accepted_version 1 yields v1.
required_output_fields.accepted_memory_status: Main lifecycle value at the first successful import acceptance. It is an immutable acceptance-receipt snapshot, not a current-state field.
required_output_fields.source_event_id: Main-resolved admitted same-user source event identity.
required_output_fields.replayed: True only when an identical idempotent logical import returned the existing production identity.

rejected_record_result.transport_failure: A request-level authentication, manifest-integrity, or JSONL framing failure returns no per-record acceptance result and is reported as a failed import command, not as a rejected record.

knowledge_id.generation: Opaque server-generated identifier allocated before calling db.repositories.insert_knowledge_entry; no format is exposed as a Data contract.
knowledge_id.stability: Stable across readback, lifecycle changes, and idempotent replay for the same logical knowledge item.

memory_id.mapping: decimal string of the SQLite memory_entries.id row that carries the knowledge_id
memory_id.stability: Stable for that persisted row and returned only by Main.

version.purpose: Content and index version, not the optimistic-concurrency token.

acceptance_receipt_snapshot.meaning: The immutable result snapshot from the first successful import acceptance. An idempotent replay returns this snapshot even when the current row version or lifecycle state has subsequently changed.
acceptance_receipt_snapshot.current_state_boundary: Current version and lifecycle state are returned only by a separate authorized readback; they are never substituted into an import acceptance replay.

row_revision.exposure: not an import identity and not a Data input field

admission_and_idempotency.source_admission: Main resolves the referenced existing same-user source event and accepts knowledge only when that event has admission_decision=allow_extraction and its immutable source_type, source_business_status, and source_reference equal the submitted descriptor. This import contract never creates a source event or fabricates provenance/security metadata. A failed source may create only failure_experience knowledge; partial, cancelled, timeout, and ignored sources are rejected.

canonical_request_sha256.canonicalization: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme followed by UTF-8 encoding
canonical_request_sha256.missing_optional_field_rule: For every optional projection field that is absent, omit the property rather than substituting null.

idempotency_registry.atomicity: Main persists this mapping in the same production transaction as source admission and knowledge creation, before reporting acceptance.

replay_result_semantics.rule: A retry with the same key and identical canonical request hash returns the first successful acceptance-receipt snapshot with replayed=true. It never substitutes a later version or lifecycle state, and it does not allocate another knowledge_id or create another row, relation, or outbox event.

durable_retention.request_cache_relation: The registry must not reuse or degrade to idempotency_cache, whose (user_id, session_id, idempotency_key) entries expire after 24 hours.
durable_retention.minimum_retention: Retain the registry and its first-success receipt snapshot for the full audit and production-identity retention lifetime of the referenced knowledge record.
durable_retention.terminal_lifecycle: removed, expired, and superseded do not release or rewrite the key. A matching replay still returns the original acceptance-receipt snapshot and a mismatched replay remains idempotency_conflict.
durable_retention.gc_boundary: No TTL-based or lifecycle-only GC is permitted. Physical GC is allowed only when an authorized Main retention policy permanently purges the referenced production identity and every audit/receipt record that could require replay recovery; the registry entry and receipt snapshot must be purged atomically with that policy action.

idempotency_registry.conflict: Reuse of the key with a different canonical request hash or data_record_id is rejected as idempotency_conflict.

manifest_record_registry.stored_value: canonical_request_sha256 and the first-success acceptance-receipt snapshot
manifest_record_registry.retention: The manifest-record registry follows the durable import identity registry retention and GC boundary; it has no request-cache TTL.
manifest_record_registry.behavior: The same manifest record with the same canonical request is replayed through its stored acceptance-receipt snapshot. The same key with a different request hash is rejected as duplicate_data_record. The key is stored atomically with the idempotency registry.

admission_and_idempotency.duplicate_policy: The per-record idempotency registry and manifest-record registry are the external replay boundaries. The repository-level same knowledge_id/source_event_id immutable replay check is a second Main-internal guard after the registry has recovered the allocated knowledge_id.
admission_and_idempotency.cross_user_policy: Lookup, replay, update, and readback are all scoped by user_id. Cross-user identity probing and reuse are rejected.

authorized_current_state_readback.meaning: Only this authorized readback represents the current row state. Import acceptance and idempotent replay represent the first-success acceptance-receipt snapshot.

update_version_delete_lifecycle.update: Main alone authorizes and performs updates. A content or index identity change advances the current version and returns a new current_version_id through authorized readback while retaining knowledge_id and memory_id. Lifecycle-only changes advance row_revision but do not rewrite the current version. Neither change rewrites a previously stored import acceptance-receipt snapshot.
update_version_delete_lifecycle.superseded: memory_status=superseded is a Main lifecycle state. If a successor is established, Main records the relationship; Data must not infer a successor from IDs.
update_version_delete_lifecycle.expired: memory_status=expired is Main-controlled and remains observable for authorized readback but is not eligible for normal retrieval.
update_version_delete_lifecycle.removed: Removal is a Main-controlled soft delete: memory_status becomes removed and the record is excluded from normal reads and retrieval. The identity is retained only for authorized audit and receipt linkage.
update_version_delete_lifecycle.id_reuse: A removed, expired, or superseded identity is never reallocated to a new Data record.

failure_contract.atomicity: Each record either yields the complete required acceptance-receipt snapshot or yields a structured rejection; no partial production identity is returned.
failure_contract.no_fallback: The importer never maps unknown values to defaults, never converts Data-local IDs into production IDs, and never reports an unexecuted import as accepted.
